universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: UMIs/cell > 1000. Low-input Flex libraries legitimately
yield 200-500 UMIs/cell. MultiQC/nf-core flags these as FAIL.
notes: 10x Flex is designed for degraded/low-input samples; low UMI is expected

universal_threshold_problem:
Smart-seq3 on sorted single cells: <1000 reads/cell in some samples.
Standard threshold: reads/cell > 5000. Flagged as low quality.
notes: Smart-seq3 on very sparse populations — low reads expected

universal_threshold_problem:
FFPE spatial transcriptomics: high technical variation + degradation signal.
Universal: genes/spot > 200. FFPE visium may have 50-150 genes/spot.
notes: FFPE spatial has lower sensitivity; fewer genes/spot is expected

universal_threshold_problem:
FFPE RNA-seq: high degradation index (DV200 < 50%), high rRNA%, high duplication.
Universal thresholds: DV200 > 70%, rRNA < 10%. Almost all FFPE samples fail.
notes: FFPE degradation is expected; DV200 < 50% is acceptable for FFPE

universal_threshold_problem:
10-year-old FFPE block: extreme degradation, high 3'-bias, low unique reads.
Universal: 5'/3' ratio < 2. This sample has ratio ~8. Universal: FAIL.
notes: Very old FFPE — data is still scientifically valid for selected genes

universal_threshold_problem:
Dataset has paired FFPE and fresh-frozen from same tumor.
Without protocol awareness, FFPE samples flagged FAIL, fresh-frozen PASS.
Naive comparison would exclude all FFPE samples from DE analysis.
notes: Paired design — FFPE should be retained with protocol-aware QC

universal_threshold_problem:
TiO2 phosphopeptide enrichment: lower total peptide coverage (enrichment
depletes non-phospho peptides). Universal: coverage > 70%. Enriched: ~20-40%.
notes: Phosphoenrichment intentionally reduces overall peptide coverage

universal_threshold_problem:
Serum depletion removes 14 high-abundance proteins (~95% of mass).
Universal: dynamic range threshold based on full serum. Post-depletion
samples appear to have very low peptide counts → FAIL.
notes: Depletion reduces apparent peptide count; true dynamic range improved

universal_threshold_problem:
Ub-remnant (diGly) enrichment: only ubiquitinated peptides recovered.
Universal peptide coverage threshold: FAIL. This is by design.
notes: PTM enrichment protocols always have low overall coverage — expected

universal_threshold_problem:
Detergent-solubilized membrane protein: high background from micelle belt.
Universal: particle contrast > 0.15. Membrane protein in micelle: ~0.05-0.10.
CTF fitting also affected by detergent ring.
notes: Membrane protein signal is inherently lower contrast; expected with detergent

universal_threshold_problem:
Nanodisc-reconstituted protein: background from lipid disc.
Universal threshold on particle score: fails. Nanodisc particles score lower.

Small membrane protein (<100 kDa in nanodisc): very low contrast.
Universal particle picking confidence threshold: too strict for small proteins.
notes: Small proteins require relaxed picking thresholds

universal_threshold_problem:
H3K27me3 broad mark: very diffuse signal, low enrichment vs input.
Universal FRiP (fraction reads in peaks) threshold > 0.3. Broad marks: FRiP ~0.05-0.15.
notes: Broad histone marks have lower FRiP by nature; ENCODE allows ≥0.05 for broad

universal_threshold_problem:
ChIP-seq from <10,000 cells: lower sequencing depth and enrichment.
Universal: library complexity (NRF > 0.8). Low-input ChIP: NRF ~0.5-0.7.

16S from stool: high host DNA contamination (up to 50%).
Universal: human mapping < 10%. Clinical stool samples often 30-60% human.
notes: Clinical stool samples routinely have high host contamination — expected

universal_threshold_problem:
CSF (cerebrospinal fluid) metagenomics: extremely low microbial biomass.
Universal: reads mapped to microbial DB > 1%. CSF: often <0.01%.
The few microbial reads present are diagnostically important.
notes: Low biomass is the expected feature of CSF; even 10 microbial reads matter

universal_threshold_problem:
ATAC-seq on frozen tissue (not fresh cells): higher mitochondrial reads,
lower TSS enrichment score. Universal TSS enrichment > 6; frozen tissue: 3-5.
notes: Frozen tissue ATAC has lower but acceptable TSS enrichment

universal_threshold_problem:
Neutrophil ATAC-seq: very condensed chromatin, fewer accessible regions.
Universal: number of peaks > 50,000. Neutrophils: 5,000-15,000 peaks.
This is biologically expected (neutrophils have limited open chromatin).
notes: Granulocyte lineage cells are chromatin-condensed; low peak count is expected

universal_threshold_problem: None — this is a genuinely defective sample
notes:
Synthetic defect: rRNA contamination 45% injected into ENCSR000AED.
Both universal and protocol-aware thresholds should correctly FAIL this.
This validates that BioMate does not over-correct toward PASS.

universal_threshold_problem: None — this is a genuinely defective sample
notes:
Synthetic defect: all cells have identical UMI barcodes (sequencing error).
Both thresholds should FAIL — tests that BioMate doesn't let everything through.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: percent mitochondrial reads < 5%. snRNA-seq from frozen
nuclei legitimately yields 0-1% mito reads (cytoplasm excluded). Tools flag
low-mito cells as stressed/dying or as ambient RNA contamination.
notes:
Nuclear isolation removes cytoplasmic mRNA including mitochondrial transcripts.
Near-zero mito% is the expected signature of quality snRNA-seq, not a defect.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: ambient RNA contamination (SoupX rho) < 0.10. Frozen
post-mortem brain tissue often yields rho 0.15-0.25 due to cell lysis during
dissection. DoubletFinder also flags more cells as doublets in high-rho samples.
notes:
Post-mortem tissue has elevated ambient RNA from lysed cells during thawing.
Correction (SoupX) is appropriate; blanket removal of all high-rho samples is not.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: UMIs/nucleus > 1000. Kidney tubular cells have compact
nuclei with limited cytoplasmic RNA. Proximal tubule nuclei: 300-700 UMIs.
Scanpy doublet detection rate inflated in dense nuclear clusters.
notes:
Kidney nuclei are smaller than cortical neurons; lower UMI counts are expected
and do not indicate failed capture.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: genes/nucleus > 500. Cardiomyocytes are binucleate and
large; nuclear isolation from cardiac tissue yields 200-450 unique genes/nucleus.
Standard QC removes most cardiomyocyte nuclei, leaving only non-cardiomyocyte cells.
notes:
Cardiomyocyte nuclei consistently fail standard UMI/gene thresholds despite
representing the majority of cardiac mass; protocol-aware profile retains them.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal doublet threshold: <5% expected doublets. Tissue dissociation of
dense tissue (e.g., solid tumors, liver) with snRNA-seq commonly yields 8-15%
predicted doublet rate. Scrublet flags large fractions of real cells.
notes:
Doublet detection tools are calibrated for well-dispersed single-cell suspensions;
dense tissues require tissue-specific expected doublet rates.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: ADT counts/cell > 100. Protein capture efficiency in
CITE-seq varies by antibody clone. CD56 (NCAM) typically yields 20-60 ADT
counts/cell in NK cells. Tools flag these as failed ADT libraries.
notes:
ADT capture efficiency is antibody-specific; low counts for low-abundance
surface proteins do not indicate library failure.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal signal-to-background: ADT signal/isotype > 3. Isotype controls for
some lineage markers (e.g., CD45) show near-saturated background in whole blood
because all leukocytes express CD45. Signal/isotype ratio < 2 flagged as FAIL.
notes:
Isotype ratio threshold is invalid for universally expressed antigens; separate
protein-specific background correction (e.g., DSB normalization) must be applied.

universal_threshold_problem:
10x Multiome ATAC+RNA: ATAC TSS enrichment threshold > 4. RNA-matched nuclei in
multiome libraries show TSS enrichment 2-3 (lower than standalone ATAC-seq)
because fixation required for multiome reduces signal. ATAC QC incorrectly fails.
notes:
10x Multiome requires permeabilization conditions optimized for dual-capture that
compromise ATAC signal strength relative to standalone ATAC-seq libraries.

universal_threshold_problem:
Cell hashing (HTO): HTO signal-to-noise threshold. Cells from primary tissue
(non-immortalized) absorb fewer hashtag oligonucleotides. HTO counts 30-80
vs. cell-line baseline >200. Demultiplexing algorithms call many as negatives.
notes:
HTO signal strength varies by cell type; primary tissue cells are particularly
prone to low HTO signal; negative call rate must be calibrated per cell type.

universal_threshold_problem:
10x Multiome RNA: genes/nucleus threshold > 500. When ATAC signal is high in
multiome, RNA capture can be reduced due to competing lysis conditions. Some
nuclei show 200-400 RNA genes but excellent ATAC profiles. RNA QC fails them.
notes:
Multiome RNA yield is systematically lower than standalone snRNA-seq; cells
with strong ATAC profiles but modest RNA should not be filtered on RNA alone.

universal_threshold_problem:
Bulk ATAC-seq: nucleosome periodicity visible as ~200 bp fragment ladder.
Thymus primary tissue: condensed chromatin shows weaker periodicity vs.
cell lines. Fragment size distribution QC (sub-200 bp fraction < 50%) fails.
notes:
Primary tissue chromatin is more compacted than cultured cells; the sub-nucleosomal
fragment fraction varies by tissue type and does not indicate library failure.

universal_threshold_problem:
Bulk ATAC-seq on brain cortex homogenate: TSS enrichment score 3-4 (threshold > 6).
Heterogeneous cell types (neurons, glia, microglia) dilute TSS signal compared
to pure cell populations. ATACseqQC and ArchR flag this as low-quality.
notes:
Cell-type heterogeneity in bulk ATAC dilutes TSS enrichment; tissue-specific
TSS thresholds are required rather than cell-line calibrated values.

universal_threshold_problem:
Bulk ATAC-seq with 10,000 cells (low): library complexity (NRF) 0.5-0.65.
Universal NRF > 0.8. Low cell input reduces unique molecule diversity leading
to higher PCR duplication rate. Flagged as poor complexity.
notes:
Low-input ATAC-seq has higher duplication by design; NRF threshold should be
relaxed for <50,000 cell inputs.

universal_threshold_problem:
ATAC-seq on FFPE-adjacent tissue sections: fragmentation is more random, peak
signal-to-background ratio reduced to 4-6 (universal threshold > 10).
Formalin crosslinking reduces transposase efficiency.
notes:
ATAC-seq from FFPE-adjacent or partially-fixed tissue has reduced Tn5 efficiency;
lower signal-to-background is expected and does not invalidate peak calls.

universal_threshold_problem:
H3K9me3 heterochromatin mark: ultra-broad enrichment domains, FRiP ~0.03-0.08.
Universal FRiP > 0.3 flags this as failed. ENCODE narrow-peak calling also
misrepresents broad heterochromatin blocks as absent.
notes:
Constitutive heterochromatin marks have very low FRiP because signal is spread
over megabase domains; MACS2 broad mode is required and FRiP threshold must be ≥0.03.

universal_threshold_problem:
H3K27me3 ChIP with older lot antibody: IP efficiency 15-25% (vs. >50% expected).
Phantom peak score (SPP NSC) 1.02 (threshold > 1.05). Flagged as failed IP.
True biology still captured — differential enrichment in Polycomb domains valid.
notes:
Antibody lot variation is common for H3K27me3; NSC/RSC thresholds are guides
not hard cutoffs — domain-level enrichment may still be biologically informative.

universal_threshold_problem:
ChIP-seq for low-occupancy TF (CTCF in resting B cells): number of called peaks
~5,000 (universal threshold > 20,000). B cells have fewer CTCF-bound sites than
fibroblasts. Flagged as insufficient enrichment.
notes:
Peak count thresholds are calibrated to reference cell lines; immune cell ChIP
routinely yields fewer peaks due to biology, not technical failure.

universal_threshold_problem:
CUT&RUN with 1,000 cells: fragment size distribution differs from ChIP-seq
(protected fragments ~150 bp, not nucleosome ladder). Universal ChIP QC
flags missing nucleosome periodicity as library failure.
notes:
CUT&RUN generates a distinct fragment size profile (short protected fragments)
compared to ChIP-seq; ChIP-centric QC tools incorrectly flag this as low quality.

universal_threshold_problem:
10x Visium spatial transcriptomics: UMIs/spot threshold > 500. Fresh-frozen
mouse brain Visium: white matter spots have 50-200 UMIs due to low cell density.
Universal filter removes anatomically valid white matter regions.
notes:
Low-cellularity regions (white matter, connective tissue) legitimately have fewer
UMIs per spot; spatial QC must use spatially-aware filters not global thresholds.

universal_threshold_problem:
Visium FFPE on tumor section: genes/spot threshold > 200. FFPE degradation
yields 80-150 genes/spot in necrotic tumor core, 300-500 in viable tumor edge.
Global QC removes entire necrotic core — scientifically important region.
notes:
Spatial heterogeneity in tumors creates systematic QC disparities; necrotic regions
have valid spatial coordinates but lower library complexity.

universal_threshold_problem:
Visium on uneven tissue section: spots at tissue edge have partial cell coverage.
Tissue detection algorithms remove spots with < 50% tissue coverage. High-quality
boundary spots at tumor-stroma interface are incorrectly removed.
notes:
Tissue edge spots have partial coverage by design; removing all edge spots
eliminates biologically critical transition zones.

universal_threshold_problem:
Visium on archival surgical biopsy: RNA quality index (RQI) 3-4 (threshold > 7).
10x SpaceRanger issues low-quality warning. Despite degradation, spatial patterns
of highly expressed genes (oncogenes, immune markers) are preserved and valid.
notes:
Partially degraded spatial samples retain spatial information for abundant
transcripts; complete rejection based on RQI discards useful spatial data.

universal_threshold_problem:
Oxford Nanopore R9.4.1 chemistry: mean read quality Q10-12. Illumina-calibrated
QC (universal Phred threshold > Q30) flags all nanopore reads as failed.
NanoPlot correctly interprets Q10 as normal for R9.4.1 pore.
notes:
Nanopore sequencing error rates are fundamentally different from Illumina; Q10
(90% accuracy) is the expected baseline for R9.4.1 chemistry, not a quality failure.

universal_threshold_problem:
Nanopore direct RNA sequencing: read length distribution skewed (mean 500 bp,
tail to 12 kb). Universal RNA-seq QC expects tight Gaussian around insert size.
Bimodal distribution flagged as contamination or fragmentation artifact.
notes:
Direct RNA-seq read length distribution reflects native mRNA length heterogeneity;
a bimodal distribution indicating short vs. long transcripts is expected.

universal_threshold_problem:
Nanopore amplicon sequencing (e.g., full-length 16S): all reads ~1.5 kb.
Universal diversity-based read length QC flags lack of diversity as library bias.
For amplicon panels this is by design.
notes:
Amplicon sequencing produces reads of defined length by design; a monodisperse
read length distribution is the expected QC signature, not a failure.

universal_threshold_problem:
Nanopore R10.4.1 duplex chemistry: ~50% reads are duplex (Q25-30), ~50% simplex
(Q12-15). Universal mean quality computed over all reads = Q18-20, flagged as
below Q30 threshold. Duplex reads are high-quality; mixed QC is misleading.
notes:
Duplex nanopore runs produce a bimodal quality distribution; global mean quality
masks the high-quality duplex fraction that is suitable for variant calling.

universal_threshold_problem:
WGBS bisulfite conversion rate: universal threshold > 99%. Placenta tissue has
low-methylation domains where incomplete conversion looks like a spike in
non-CpG methylation. Bismark QC reports conversion 97.5%, triggers FAIL.
notes:
Placental and early embryonic samples have unusual methylation landscapes that
can lower apparent bisulfite conversion rate; tissue context is critical for QC.

universal_threshold_problem:
Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) WGBS: fragment length 160-180 bp (nucleosome-protected).
Universal WGBS expected insert size 300-500 bp. cfDNA shows tight nucleosomal
sizing which universal QC flags as over-fragmentation.
notes:
cfDNA WGBS fragment size distribution reflects nucleosome-protected circulating
DNA; nucleosomal sizing (~167 bp) is the expected cfDNA signature.

universal_threshold_problem:
Reduced Representation Bisulfite Sequencing (RRBS): genome coverage ~4-8%.
Universal bisulfite QC checks genome-wide CpG coverage (threshold > 30%).
RRBS by design only covers MspI-digested CpG-rich fragments; 4-8% is correct.
notes:
RRBS achieves deep local coverage of ~4-8% of CpG sites; genome-wide coverage
metrics are inapplicable and will always flag RRBS as failing.

universal_threshold_problem:
WGBS in pluripotent stem cells: CH methylation (non-CpG) 20-30%. Universal QC
checks CH methylation < 5% as a proxy for bisulfite conversion quality.
Stem cells and neurons have high CH methylation biologically.
notes:
Non-CpG methylation is a genuine biological feature of neurons and stem cells;
using CH methylation as a conversion quality proxy fails for these cell types.

universal_threshold_problem:
Smart-seq2 full-length scRNA-seq: reads per cell 100,000-500,000, uniform across
gene body (no 3' bias). Universal droplet-based QC expects 3'-biased read
distribution; Smart-seq2 even coverage flagged as ribo-seq contamination.
notes:
Smart-seq2 produces full-length cDNA with even gene body coverage; 3'-bias metrics
are inapplicable and will flag high-quality Smart-seq2 data as aberrant.

universal_threshold_problem:
Smart-seq2 on sorted rare cells: 50,000-80,000 reads/cell (budget plate).
Universal reads/cell threshold > 250,000. Low-depth Smart-seq2 captures most
highly expressed genes but flags fail on depth.
notes:
Smart-seq2 read depth requirements depend on cell type and scientific question;
50k reads captures the expressed transcriptome of small cells adequately.

universal_threshold_problem:
Smart-seq2 with ERCC spike-ins: spike-in fraction 10-25% of total reads.
Universal QC: spike-in fraction < 5% (treats spikes as contamination).
ERCC spike-ins are intentionally added for normalization; high fraction expected.
notes:
ERCC spike-in fraction must be interpreted in context of spike-in dilution;
a 10-25% ERCC fraction is normal for the recommended 1:20 dilution in Smart-seq2.

universal_threshold_problem:
Total RNA-seq with Ribo-Zero depletion: rRNA fraction 2-8% residual after
depletion. Universal polyA-seq rRNA threshold < 1%. Ribo-Zero efficiency is
lower than polyA selection; 2-8% residual is the normal operating range.
notes:
Ribo-Zero depletion is less efficient than polyA selection; 2-8% residual rRNA
is the expected range and does not indicate failed depletion.

universal_threshold_problem:
Total RNA-seq targeting lncRNA: lower coding gene coverage, higher intronic
reads (lncRNAs are less efficiently spliced). Universal: intronic reads < 30%.
Total RNA-seq typically shows 40-60% intronic reads; lncRNA-enriched samples higher.
notes:
lncRNA-focused total RNA-seq has higher intronic read fractions than mRNA-seq;
intronic read thresholds calibrated on polyA libraries are inapplicable.

universal_threshold_problem:
Total RNA-seq from bacteria: no poly-A tails, no splicing, all reads map to
coding or rRNA genes. Universal eukaryotic QC checks for splicing junction
reads > 30% and flags 0% junctions as alignment failure.
notes:
Prokaryotic RNA-seq has no splice junctions; eukaryotic splicing-based QC
metrics are fundamentally inapplicable to bacterial transcriptomics.

universal_threshold_problem:
10x Genomics TCR V(D)J sequencing: >95% of reads map to V(D)J loci.
Universal QC: reads mapping to reference genome > 80% on other loci.
V(D)J libraries are targeted enrichments — near-100% V(D)J mapping is correct.
notes:
V(D)J sequencing is an amplicon enrichment of immunoglobulin/TCR loci; non-VDJ
reference mapping of <5% is the expected signature of high-quality libraries.

universal_threshold_problem:
BCR V(D)J from tumor-infiltrating B cells: very low clonotype diversity (clonal
expansion). Shannon entropy < 1 (universal threshold > 3). Flagged as poor
library complexity, but clonal dominance is the expected biology in tumors.
notes:
Clonal expansion is the hallmark of antigen-driven immune responses; low
clonotype diversity in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes is biologically expected.

universal_threshold_problem:
TCR V(D)J paired alpha-beta sequencing: ~60-75% of cells have both chains
detected. Universal cell pairing threshold > 90%. Low-pairing rate in primary
tissue is due to RNA accessibility not library failure.
notes:
TCR chain pairing rate depends on cell activation state and RNA quality;
60-75% pairing in primary tissue is acceptable and biologically informative.

universal_threshold_problem: None — this is a genuinely defective sample
notes:
Synthetic defect: pore blockage event injected — 80% of reads are <50 bp
(failed pore runs). Both universal and protocol-aware QC should correctly FAIL.
Validates that nanopore profile does not over-correct toward PASS.

universal_threshold_problem: None — this is a genuinely defective sample
notes:
Synthetic defect: bisulfite conversion rate 78% (genuine under-conversion,
not tissue-specific). High false-methylation rate. Both thresholds should FAIL.

universal_threshold_problem: None — this is a genuinely defective sample
notes:
Synthetic defect: input DNA sequenced without any IP step (no enrichment).
FRiP = 0.001. Even with broad-mark profile, this should FAIL — no signal present.

universal_threshold_problem:
snRNA-seq from aged mouse brain: genes/nucleus 200-350 (threshold > 500).
Aged neurons show transcriptional quiescence with reduced mRNA output.
Universal QC removes >70% of aged neuronal nuclei.
notes:
Transcriptional quiescence in aged neurons produces genuinely low gene counts;
WARN is appropriate — retain with annotation of reduced sensitivity.

universal_threshold_problem:
Visium on small biopsy punch: 200 spots under tissue (threshold > 1000 spots).
Small tissue sections are clinically common (core biopsy, surgical margin).
SpaceRanger warns on <500 spots. Spatial patterns are valid despite small area.
notes:
Total spot count reflects tissue area not library quality; small biopsies are
clinically important and valid for spatial analysis at reduced resolution.

universal_threshold_problem:
CITE-seq from PBMCs with suboptimal wash: ADT background 30-50% of signal
(universal signal/background threshold > 5). DSB normalization corrects for
this; raw ADT counts flagged but normalized values interpretable.
notes:
High ADT background from imperfect washing is recoverable with DSB normalization;
raw count QC failure does not necessarily mean protein data is unusable.

universal_threshold_problem:
Bulk ATAC-seq on circulating neutrophils: 3,000-8,000 peaks (threshold > 30,000).
Neutrophils have highly condensed chromatin and limited open chromatin accessible
to Tn5. Used for neutrophil activation studies comparing treated vs. untreated.
notes:
Granulocyte chromatin compaction produces genuinely low peak counts; the relevant
comparison is treated vs. untreated neutrophils, not neutrophils vs. T cells.

universal_threshold_problem:
Smart-seq2 on circulating tumor cells (CTCs): 30,000-60,000 reads/cell.
CTCs are extremely rare, captured singly; budget sequencing unavoidable.
Universal reads/cell > 250,000 flags entire CTC dataset as FAIL.
notes:
CTC studies often operate with low sequencing depth per cell due to rarity of
material; modest depth still captures clinically informative gene expression.

universal_threshold_problem:
RRBS from FFPE: duplication rate 60-80% (universal threshold < 40%).
RRBS on FFPE is a double-enrichment: restriction digest + bisulfite conversion
on degraded DNA → very limited unique molecules, high duplication expected.
notes:
RRBS from FFPE has constrained unique molecule diversity; deduplication removes
too much signal. Protocol-aware QC should flag WARN and recommend dedup-aware analysis.

universal_threshold_problem:
Total RNA-seq optimized for circular RNA detection: RNase R treatment degrades
linear RNA, enriching circular species. Linear RNA fraction 20-30% (from
incomplete RNase R treatment). Standard QC flags 30% unmapped reads (back-splice
junctions not in standard annotation) as alignment failure.
notes:
circRNA studies require back-splice-aware aligners (STAR with chimeric options or
find_circ); standard junction QC is inapplicable to circRNA-enriched libraries.

universal_threshold_problem:
gamma-delta T cell TCR V(D)J sequencing: <20% of reads have productive
rearrangements (threshold > 60%). gamma-delta TCRs are less efficiently
captured by V(D)J enrichment oligos optimized for alpha-beta TCRs.
notes:
10x V(D)J enrichment is optimized for alpha-beta TCRs; gamma-delta TCRs have
lower capture efficiency by design and require adjusted productivity thresholds.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: genes/spot > 500. Visium spots on white matter or necrotic
tissue legitimately yield 50-200 genes/spot. MultiQC flags low-coverage spots as
low-quality without tissue context.
notes:
White matter is transcriptionally sparse; low gene counts per spot are biologically
expected, not technical failure. Tissue mask and histology context are required.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: mean read quality > Q20. Oxford Nanopore direct RNA reads
yield Q8-Q12 median quality. Guppy high-accuracy basecalling improves this to
Q12-Q15, still far below Illumina Q30 thresholds.
notes:
Direct RNA sequencing on R9.4.1 or R10.4 flowcells has inherently lower per-base
accuracy than cDNA; Q10 is the accepted quality floor for this chemistry.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: PCR duplicate rate < 20%. MAGeCK CRISPR screens use PCR
amplification with degenerate primers; duplicate rates of 40-70% are normal and
expected in high-representation screens.
notes:
CRISPR screen libraries are deliberately over-represented; high PCR duplicate
rates reflect library complexity preservation, not contamination.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: mapped read pairs > 80%. Hi-C libraries have 40-60%
valid ligation products; chimeric read pairs from non-adjacent restriction
fragments are expected and removed by HiC-Pro at the pipeline level.
notes:
Hi-C valid pair rate of 40-60% is standard; "unmapped" pairs often represent
dangling ends and self-circles that are correctly filtered downstream.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: CV% < 20% across all features. Lipid species and secondary
metabolites in LC-MS untargeted metabolomics often show CV 30-50% due to
biological variation, not analytical failure.
notes:
High CV for low-abundance metabolites is expected biologically; QC pool CV < 20%
is the correct metric, not per-feature CV across biological samples.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: empty droplet rate > 5% = FAIL. SoupX/CellBender-corrected
10x libraries report 10-25% ambient RNA contamination as PASSED data, which raw
QC tools incorrectly flag before correction is applied.
notes:
Ambient RNA contamination at 10-25% is correctable; the flag should be raised
only if contamination exceeds 40% or if correction artifacts are present.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: clonotype entropy > 3.0 (diverse). Tumor-infiltrating T cells
in clonally expanded responses show entropy 0.5-1.5, which naive QC flags as
"low diversity / poor library" rather than biologically significant clonal expansion.
notes:
Low clonotype entropy in TIL samples is a biological signal of antigen-driven
clonal expansion, not a sequencing quality issue.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: reads/cell > 500,000. Rare cell populations in Smart-seq2
at 1:1000 dilution yield 50,000-150,000 reads/cell when cell numbers are low,
as total sequencing depth is spread across the whole plate.
notes:
Smart-seq2 plate depth varies by cell loading; rare population isolation plates
have fewer total cells and thus lower per-cell sequencing depth by design.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: ATAC TSS enrichment > 7. 10x Multiome ATAC+RNA co-captured
nuclei yield TSS enrichment of 4-6, below single-assay ATAC thresholds, because
the GEM-X chemistry is optimized for dual-capture not maximal ATAC sensitivity.
notes:
Multiome ATAC inherently has lower TSS enrichment than dedicated ATAC-seq due to
shared GEM volume; adjusted thresholds of 3-5 are appropriate for this assay.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: rRNA reads < 5%. Ribo-zero depleted PBMC total RNA-seq
retains 8-15% rRNA in blood-derived samples due to incomplete depletion of the
globin-abundant erythrocyte rRNA fraction.
notes:
Ribo-depletion efficiency in blood samples is lower than in tissue RNA due to
high globin and rRNA abundance; 8-15% residual rRNA is acceptable.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: library complexity (NRF) > 0.9. CUT&RUN with 5,000 cells
yields NRF 0.6-0.75 due to limited input chromatin; standard ChIP-seq NRF
thresholds assume millions of cells.
notes:
Low-cell CUT&RUN and CUT&TAG protocols operate on 1,000-50,000 cells; library
complexity thresholds must be adjusted proportionally to input cell number.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: UMIs/nucleus > 1,000. Cardiac muscle nuclei in snRNA-seq
yield 500-800 UMIs due to compact nuclear volume and low cytoplasmic RNA
contamination in post-mortem heart tissue.
notes:
Post-mortem cardiac tissue has reduced RNA integrity; low UMI counts per nucleus
are expected and do not indicate failed library preparation.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: fraction reads in peaks (FRiP) > 0.2. FFPE ATAC-seq
yields FRiP 0.05-0.12 due to crosslinking-induced chromatin compaction and
fragmentation artefacts from formalin fixation.
notes:
FFPE ATAC is inherently noisier; FRiP 0.08-0.12 is acceptable for FFPE material
and should trigger a WARN, not FAIL, with a note on fixation.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: mean read N50 > 10 kb. PacBio HiFi (CCS) reads average
15-20 kb N50 by design, but raw CLR reads in older protocols average 5-8 kb
N50, which naive QC incorrectly flags as short-insert contamination.
notes:
CLR vs CCS protocol determines expected read length distribution; N50 thresholds
must be calibrated to the specific PacBio chemistry used.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: CpG coverage uniformity > 0.8. RRBS by design captures
only restriction-proximal CpGs; coverage uniformity across the genome is 0.2-0.4,
correctly reflecting the enrichment design, not a failure.
notes:
RRBS is an enrichment protocol; non-uniform genome coverage is the expected and
correct outcome, not a QC failure. Uniformity should be measured within RRBS
target regions only.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: protein (ADT) UMIs/cell > 200. CITE-seq with isotype
control antibodies included in the panel shows 50-100 total ADT UMIs/cell for
low-abundance surface markers while isotype controls show 5-20 UMIs.
notes:
ADT counts depend on surface marker abundance; low-expression markers like
CD34 or CD56 in non-hematopoietic contexts legitimately yield low ADT UMIs.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: nucleosome-free region (NFR) fraction > 0.4. Bulk ATAC-seq
from laser-capture microdissected samples (100-1000 cells) yields NFR 0.25-0.35
due to limited Tn5 tagmentation efficiency at low cell numbers.
notes:
Low-input bulk ATAC requires adjusted NFR thresholds; the nucleosomal periodicity
pattern is more diagnostic than the NFR absolute fraction for these samples.

FFPE RNA is inherently degraded; RIN 2-4 is the expected range and should
trigger a WARN (with degradation note) rather than hard FAIL.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: doublet rate < 5%. 10x Genomics high-throughput loading
at 20,000 cells/well yields 10-15% doublet rate by design; this is acceptable
and handled by Scrublet/DoubletFinder post-processing.
notes:
High-throughput 10x loading intentionally allows higher doublet rates in exchange
for more cells recovered; computational doublet removal is the expected workflow.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: imputation R² > 0.3. Rare variant GWAS (MAF < 0.5%) with
array-based imputation yields R² 0.1-0.25 for variants in low-LD regions.
PLINK/IMPUTE2 flag these as poor quality though they may be well-imputed given
the sparse LD structure.
notes:
Rare variant imputation quality depends on reference panel density and regional
LD; blanket R² > 0.3 filters remove legitimate rare variant associations.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: phosphopeptide enrichment efficiency > 80%. TiO₂ or IMAC
enrichment of phosphopeptides from complex lysates yields 60-75% efficiency when
starting material is < 100 µg protein, which mass spec QC tools flag as poor.
notes:
Phospho enrichment efficiency is input-dependent; < 100 µg protein input is
expected to yield lower efficiency, and 60-75% is acceptable for clinical samples.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: TMT labeling efficiency > 95%. Clinical biopsy samples
with limited protein yield achieve 85-92% TMT labeling efficiency; standard
proteomics QC tools flag this as incomplete labeling failure.
notes:
TMT labeling efficiency < 95% is acceptable for limited clinical samples;
unlabeled peptides can be identified and excluded computationally.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: length distribution CV < 0.3 (monodisperse). Nanopore
amplicon panels from 16S/18S/ITS targets yield monodisperse length distributions
(CV < 0.1), which some QC tools flag as "amplicon contamination" due to lack
of length variation.
notes:
Targeted amplicon sequencing should produce a monodisperse length distribution;
low CV is the expected outcome of PCR amplification of a fixed-size target.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: mitochondrial reads < 10%. Metabolically active neurons
and cardiomyocytes legitimately express 20-35% mitochondrial reads; blanket
mito filters remove live, healthy cells in these lineages.
notes:
Mitochondrial read fraction thresholds are cell-type-specific; neurons and
cardiomyocytes require relaxed thresholds of 20-30% for their high energy demand.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: peak FRIP > 0.2. CUT&TAG for active histone marks
(H3K4me3) yields FRIP 0.5-0.8, but repressive marks (H3K27me3, H3K9me3)
spread across large domains yield FRIP 0.05-0.15, which is flagged as failure.
notes:
Repressive marks form broad, low-signal domains; FRIP scores must be calibrated
to the mark type, not a single universal threshold.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: spots with > 200 genes. Visium HD at 2µm resolution
yields many spots with 50-150 genes as the smaller spot size captures partial
cells; this is the intended behavior of the assay.
notes:
Visium HD uses 2×2 µm bins; each bin captures a sub-cellular area and lower
gene counts per bin are expected and informative at this resolution.

Time-series transcriptomics has structured variance by design; blind batch
correction destroys the temporal signal. Zeitgeber grouping should be
treated as a biological factor, not a batch.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: mapping rate to reference > 85%. Patient-derived xenograft
(PDX) scRNA-seq aligned to human reference alone yields 50-65% mapping rate
because mouse stromal cells (30-50% of total) map to the human genome poorly.
notes:
PDX samples require dual-species alignment; low human-reference mapping rate
is expected due to the mouse cell fraction and should trigger a WARN with
recommendation for species-deconvolution alignment.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: genes detected per cell > 200. Highly pure populations
(e.g., erythrocytes, platelets, regulatory T cells) have genuinely restricted
transcriptomes with 50-180 genes expressed; blanket filters remove these
biologically important cell types.
notes:
Mature erythrocytes and platelets are transcriptionally quiescent; low gene
counts reflect their biology, not library failure. Context-aware thresholds
based on cell clustering are appropriate.

universal_threshold_problem:
Universal threshold: percent on-target reads > 80%. Nanopore adaptive sampling
(ReadFish/Dorado) enriches target regions to 60-70% on-target in complex
genomes, rejecting off-target reads in real-time. QC tools flag 30-40% off-target
reads as enrichment failure.
notes:
Adaptive sampling enrichment efficiency of 60-70% is state-of-the-art for
real-time selective sequencing; 30-40% off-target reads are expected given
the reaction kinetics of pore-based rejection.
